import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Reading the lead report is done; next I'm reading the diagram manifest and checking the image assets.

Line break splits the phrase; adjusting the match.

The draft reads cleanly. Running the validation: anchors via pandoc, table and code-block fidelity, a word-level diff against the lead, and checks that the figure assets exist.

Every changed block is one of my intentional link insertions, and all 11 in-document link targets resolve in pandoc. Writing the canonical file without overwrite, then registering it.

Registration succeeded. Finishing the turn through `/sase_final`; the new file in the research repo needs a commit decision.

I published the lead's report as `202611/task_video_capture_z_viewer/task_video_capture_z_viewer.md` in the research repo and registered it as `research:202611/task_video_capture_z_viewer/task_video_capture_z_viewer.md` (`file:explicit:8c41a4511100743145bfa1bd`). It was written without overwrite (there was no existing file), and the commit to the research repo is declared and runs after this turn ends.

**Layout and checks**
- **Opening order:** title, then a research-query blockquote, then the infographic (`task_video_capture_z_viewer_infographic.png`, which exists beside the report), then `## Bottom line` (the lead's TL;DR).
- **Section order:** Is this a good idea → What exists today → Recommended design (bob-cli / bob-plugins / bob-mac-capture) → Requirement adjustments explicitly called out → Alternatives considered and rejected → Where the researchers disagreed and how it was resolved → Pre-existing bugs this research surfaced → Phase-0 spike → Rollout → Recommended solution → Sources. It still ends with the recommended solution, as the request asked.
- **Headings:** no hand-numbered headings and no table of contents. I moved the parenthetical parts of the lead's headings into each section's first line. The lead's opening byline (date, sources merged, scope) now opens the Sources section, since nothing may sit between the title and the query.
- **Fidelity:** all 7 tables (68 rows), both code blocks, and every paragraph match the lead's wording, except the link edits below. The lead's two SVG figures and their "Figure 1/2" captions are unchanged, and both SVG files exist.
- **Section-number links:** with the hand numbering removed, the lead's "§N" pointers would point at the wrong sections. I replaced each with an in-document link to its section. This changes the wording of two table cells: A9's "(§5)" and Rollout phase 0's "§6 spike".
- **Other links:** I added a few links from the bottom line to the sections that back it. All 11 in-document link targets resolve in `pandoc -t html`.
- **External URLs:** the lead's report had none, so nothing was unrepairable.

**Diagrams.** The image agent's status was `ready`, and the manifest's `source` matches the lead's report. I placed both diagrams byte-for-byte, so the file has 2 Mermaid fences (the lead had 0):
- `source-integrity` → `figure-source-integrity`, after the Streaming list in the bob-cli section.
- `viewer-lifecycle` → `figure-viewer-lifecycle`, after the list of viewer rules in the bob-plugins section.

Each sits in its own figure `<div>`, both IDs appear in pandoc's HTML, and each has one reference sentence linking to it. No diagrams were left out.

The image agent also registered an image, `task_capture_video_embeds_classify.png`, that the lead's report never embedded. I left it out, since only the lead decides which of its own figures appear.
